item.title: Nucleated Blood, Elementary Bodies, and Vitellogenic Calcium — Companion Bird Hematology & Lead Rubricytosis (V049), Avian Chlamydiosis 3-Site PCR & 45-Day Doxycycline (V050), Reptile Chemistry & Vitellogenesis (V051) & Reptile Coprology Traps (V052)

item.title: Gill Lamellae, Trunk Kidneys, Exhaust Dust, and Brainstems — Teleost Gill Wet Mounts & Gas Bubble Disease (V053), Aquatic Kidney Culture, 37°C Traps & FDA VFDs (V054), Lab Rodent Exhaust Air Dust PCR (V055) & Wildlife Rabies DFA & CDC LN34 RT-qPCR (V056)
item.description: One Medicine Capstone synthesis of teleost wet mounts (V053), fish bacteriology (V054), lab rodent surveillance (V055), and wildlife rabies testing (V056): 15m gill autolysis clock, buffered MS-222, Gyrodactylus vs. Dactylogyrus, and Gas Bubble Disease; Posterior Trunk Kidney culture, 15-28C thermal/TYES media, CLSI VET03/04, and FDA VFD law; IVC Exhaust Air Dust qPCR, NSG serology traps, binomial n=299 math, and LCMV biologics PCR; and bilateral Brainstem+Cerebellum DFA, CDC LN34 decomposed-brain rescue, cryptic bedroom bats, and FAVN titers.

item.description: Comparative auditory diagnostics across species (H050 & V034): Plonek's unilaterally deaf English Setter BAER waveforms and Lewis's 8,955-dog UK Dalmatian screening cohort (1,201 unilateral, 397 bilateral, 8 equivocal) paired with Starr's classic auditory neuropathy series and Eom's child with absent click ABR yet normal pure-tone thresholds and language.

item.title: The Pause That Finally Had a Time — Implantable Loop Recorder Asystole Masquerading as Epilepsy (Kanjwal 2010) vs. 38-Second Ictal Asystole on Simultaneous EEG/ECG (Nandkeolyar 2018), RAST Yield & Recorder Artifacts
item.description: Behind the Curtain of ambulatory ECG and implantable loop recording (H041): Kanjwal et al.'s (2010) loop-recorder capture of complete heart block and prolonged asystole causing convulsive syncope previously treated as epilepsy, contrasted with Nandkeolyar et al.'s (2018) simultaneous video-EEG/ECG capture of right temporal seizure onset preceding a 38-second ictal asystole, Krahn's randomized RAST diagnostic yield (14/27 vs. 6/30), and Domenichini's (2023) false-positive pause artifacts.

item.title: The Side the Scalp Could See — Simultaneous Scalp vs. Stereo-EEG Seizure Detection (Gunnell 2025), 51-Second Contralateral Scalp Lag & ICU Peripheral Nerve Stimulator EEG Artifacts
item.description: Behind the Curtain of clinical electroencephalography (H045): simultaneous intracranial stereo-EEG and scalp EEG recordings showing a 51-second delay and false contralateral lateralization on the scalp (Nandkeolyar 2018; Gunnell et al. 2025 across 172 seizures), skull/tissue attenuation of deep focal discharges, and ICU peripheral nerve stimulator train-of-four artifacts mimicking seizures (Dhakal 2017).

item.title: The Fluid With a Second Reading — Visually Clear CSF vs. Spectrophotometric Net Bilirubin Absorbance in Delayed Subarachnoid Hemorrhage, UK NEQAS Cutoffs & Traumatic Tap Differentiation
item.description: Behind the Curtain of cerebrospinal fluid analysis (H055): why visually colorless CSF Supernatant can still harbor diagnostic bilirubin absorbance at 476 nm after delayed subarachnoid hemorrhage, heme-to-bilirubin enzymatic kinetics vs. traumatic tap oxyhemoglobin artifacts, and UK national spectrophotometry guidelines.

item.title: The Movement After the Missing Breath — Video-Polysomnography (H044), Obstructive Sleep Apnea Arousal Pseudo-RBD vs. True REM Sleep Without Atonia & CPAP Resolution
item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H044) investigation of nocturnal dream-enactment mimics: how synchronized video-polysomnography (EEG, EOG, submental/limb EMG, nasal pressure, and thoracoabdominal effort belts) separates true alpha-synucleinopathy REM sleep behavior disorder (sustained/phasic REM sleep without atonia) from severe obstructive sleep apnea respiratory-arousal pseudo-RBD that resolves completely on CPAP (Deguchi et al. 2021; Bergmann et al. 2024).

item.title: The Reference Sample Had Changed — Post-Transplant Forensic DNA Chimerism Across Blood (100% Donor), Buccal Swabs (Mixed Leukocyte Infiltration) & Hair/Eyebrow Follicles
item.description: Forensic genetics of biological chimerism after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation: why blood reference samples convert completely to the donor's STR and amelogenin sex profile, why buccal swabs yield variable donor-recipient DNA mixtures due to mucosal leukocyte trafficking, and why hair shafts and eyebrow follicles remain reliable recipient reference tissues (Jacewicz et al. 2013; Li et al. 2014; 2026 eyebrow follicle study).

item.title: The Rhythm That Waited for the Treadmill — CPVT Exercise Stress ECG (H042), Post-Exertional Bidirectional VT, RYR2 Diastolic Calcium Leak & Paired-Test Repeatability
item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H042) investigation of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT): why resting ECGs and structural echocardiography are normal, how adrenergic surge and early post-exercise recovery unmask beat-to-beat alternating bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (Akiba et al. 2026), RYR2 diastolic Ca2+ leak and NCX1 delayed afterdepolarizations (Steinberg et al. 2023), and exercise-test repeatability limits (Peltenburg et al. 2023).

item.title: The Seed the Scan Could Not Name — Adult Occult Sapodilla Seed Aspiration (Nguyen Phan 2026), Two-Year Unilateral Wheeze & Flexible Bronchoscopy Extraction (H049)
item.description: Pulmonary diagnostics and flexible bronchoscopy (H049) for occult adult airway foreign bodies: Nguyen Phan et al.'s (2026) two-year missed sapodilla seed aspiration masquerading as recurrent right-lower-lobe pneumonia and asthma, radiolucent organic foreign-body CT physics, granulation-tissue tumor mimics, and flexible vs. rigid bronchoscopic retrieval across adult cohorts (Jang et al. 2022; Purohit et al. 2023).

item.title: The Clock Inside the Chest — Postmortem Pacemaker & ICD Interrogation, Cloud Telemetry Timestamps (Straw 2024) & Blinded Forensic Device Audits (Lackermair 2022)
item.description: Forensic electrophysiology of postmortem cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) interrogation: remote cloud telemetry alerts preceding body discovery (2024 Connected to the Cloud case), Lackermair et al.'s (2022) blinded forensic autopsy interrogation series, intracardiac electrogram differentiation of tachyarrhythmic vs. non-arrhythmic death, and clock-drift/electromechanical dissociation pitfalls.

item.title: The Breath the Spirometer Missed — Normal Spirometry with 31% Predicted DLCO, Plethysmographic Lung Volumes, Combined Fibrosis & Emphysema (CPFE) & ERS/ATS Standards
item.description: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H043 (Lung Volumes & Diffusing Capacity): why a patient can have FVC 112% predicted and TLC 88% predicted alongside a single-breath DLCO of 31% predicted (Neder et al. 2019), how opposing mechanical effects of emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis preserve lung volumes while destroying alveolar-capillary gas transfer (Kim et al. 2022 IPF-PRO registry, N=934; Barisione et al. 2014), and the 2017 ERS/ATS single-breath CO uptake standard (Graham et al. 2017).

item.title: The Spine That Looked Too Dense — Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) Projection Geometry, Aortic Calcification & Contrast Artifacts, Vertebral Exclusions & ISCD Positions
item.description: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H037 (DXA Bone Densitometry & Projection Artifacts): how two-energy X-ray attenuation integrates all mineral along the beam path, why an L1 vertebral compression fracture and abdominal aortic calcification produced a high anteroposterior lumbar reading (Gupta et al. 2021), iodinated contrast (+3.8 to -1.5 T-score) and vertebral cement exclusions (+7.7 to -2.6 T-score, White et al. 2025), person-level vs. vertebra-level osteophyte and fracture comparisons in 96 women (Paiva et al. 2002), and the 2023 ISCD Adult Official Positions.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed in the Scan — [18F]FDG from 1976–1979 Brain Autoradiography (Sokoloff & Reivich) and Cyclotron 109.77-Min Decay to GLUT3/Hexokinase II Trapping (4ZW9/2NZT), Thoracic SUVmax 7.2 & EBUS Granulomas
item.description: From cyclotron target to thoracic staging needle: Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]deoxyglucose method and Reivich/Alavi/Phelps's 1976-1979 human [18F]FDG brain studies, Hamacher nucleophilic synthesis and 109.77-minute half-life batch logistics (21 CFR 212.70), D-glucose-bound GLUT3 (PDB 4ZW9) and human hexokinase II (PDB 2NZT) metabolic trapping, 511-keV coincidence physics and SUVbw math (7.2 g/mL), and why bilateral FDG-avid mediastinal nodes still require EBUS-TBNA tissue confirmation (granulomatous inflammation vs. metastasis).

item.title: The Switch That Keeps Us Awake — Hypothalamic Orexin/Hypocretin Discovery, Canine HCRTR2 & Human CSF Orexin-A Deficiency in Narcolepsy Type 1, OX2R Crystal Structures (4S0V/7L1U) & Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists
item.description: From wake-maintenance physiology to targeted insomnia pharmacology: 1998 discovery of hypothalamic hypocretins/orexins, 1999 canine HCRTR2 and murine knockout narcolepsy models, human CSF orexin-A <=110 pg/mL cutoff in ICSD-3 narcolepsy type 1, structural comparison of antagonist-bound (PDB 4S0V) vs. agonist-bound (PDB 7L1U) OX2R, and clinical trials and next-morning safety of suvorexant and daridorexant.

item.title: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
item.description: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

item.title: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
item.description: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

item.title: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
item.description: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

item.title: The Signal That Outlasted the Cigarette — Exhaled CO vs. Urine Cotinine & Anabasine on Nicotine Patch, Langley's Receptor Concept, Human alpha4-beta2 nAChR Varenicline Cryo-EM (6UR8) & the EAGLES Trial
item.description: From John Newport Langley's 1905 'receptive substance' to transplant tobacco abstinence verification: human alpha4-beta2 nAChR cryo-EM structure bound to varenicline (PDB 6UR8), cytisine-to-varenicline partial agonist design, CYP2A6 nicotine-to-cotinine kinetics, LC-MS/MS separation of isobaric nicotine and minor tobacco alkaloid anabasine (m/z 163), and the 8,144-participant EAGLES trial.

item.title: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
item.description: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

item.title: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. item.title: The Vitamin the Body Couldn't Clear — PTH-Suppressed Hypercalcemia, Human VDR-Calcitriol Structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann's LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D:24,25(OH)2D Ratio & CYP24A1 Loss
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of vitamin D catabolism and CYP24A1 deficiency: why normal 25(OH)D3 with suppressed PTH and elevated 1,25(OH)2D3 points to failed 24-hydroxylase inactivation rather than overdose, the 1.8 Å human VDR-calcitriol crystal structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann & Jones's (2014) PTAD-derivatized LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D3:24,25(OH)2D3 molar ratio diagnostic (>80), and Schlingmann et al.'s (2011) discovery of idiopathic infantile and adult CYP24A1 hypercalcemia.

item.title: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

item.title: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

item.title: The Letter the First Test Missed — Compound Heterozygous DPYD Variants Missed by 4-SNP Panels (de Haar-Holleman 2024), Fluorouracil Catabolism Collapse & Uridine Triacetate Antidote Rescue
item.description: Pharmacogenomics and biochemical rescue of fluoropyrimidine toxicity: why targeted 4-variant DPYD genotyping misses rare in-trans compound heterozygotes (de Haar-Holleman et al. 2024), phenotypic DPD uracil breath/plasma assays (Coenen et al. 2019), 5-FU catabolic shunting into FUTP/FdUMP (Peters et al. 1988), and emergency antidote rescue with uridine triacetate (Jacob et al. 2022).

item.description: Structural immunology and therapeutic drug monitoring of infliximab in ulcerative colitis: chimeric cA2 engineering (Knight 1993), 2.60 Å TNF-alpha:infliximab Fab crystal structure (PDB 4G3Y, Liang 2013), transmembrane TNF bivalent avidity (Scallon 2002), ACT 1 & ACT 2 mucosal healing trials (Rutgeerts 2005), and anti-drug antibody clearance vs. assay non-interchangeability.

item.title: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. item.title: The Signal That Tested the Pituitary — Ghrelin & GOAT Discovery, Macimorelin Bound to Human GHSR–Gq (PDB 9V2N), 22-kDa GH Immunoassay & ITT Crossover Agreement
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 78: reverse pharmacology from GHSR1a cloning (Howard et al. 1996) to rat stomach ghrelin isolation (Kojima et al. 1999) and GOAT/MBOAT4 Ser3 octanoylation (Yang 2008; Gutierrez 2008), peptidomimetic macimorelin (JMV1843) bound to human GHSR-Gq at 2.63 Å (PDB 9V2N, Asp99/Arg102/Ser123), 22-kDa IDS-iSYS chemiluminescent GH assay, thorough QTcF crossover (+9.61 ms at 4 h), and 139-pair vs. 140-pair diagnostic agreement against the insulin tolerance test (Garcia et al.).

item.title: The Number After the Blood Was Cleared — Pre-Dialysis Lithium Rebound, 7Li Brain MRS Half-Life, Spent-Tank Dialysate Recovery & EXTRIP Cohort Predictions
item.description: Multi-compartment pharmacokinetics and clinical toxicology of lithium clearance: pre-dialysis serum rebound during IV hydration in chronic toxicity with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Kobylianskii et al. 2021, 1.50->0.40->1.30 mmol/L), human 7Li brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy vs. serum half-lives (Plenge et al. 1994), direct mass recovery of 250 mg lithium in collected spent dialysate vs. serum percentage reduction (Schmidt et al. 2014), and retrospective evaluation of EXTRIP dialysis criteria across 361 poisonings (Buckley et al. 2020).

item.title: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
item.description: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

item.title: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 81: neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia critical-sample diagnostics (simultaneous glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and free fatty acids; Ferrara et al.), repurposing antihypertensive benzothiadiazine diazoxide (Drash & Wolff 1964), beta-cell SUR1/Kir6.2 KATP opening and NN414 comparator structure (PDB 7W4O), dominant KCNJ11 p.Phe55Leu gating vs. recessive focal 11p15 loss, and echocardiographic surveillance for diazoxide-associated pulmonary hypertension (Herrera et al., 7/295).

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.title: How a Blood Test Tracks the Insulin Your Body Makes — Berson & Yalow's 1956–1960 Competitive 131I-Insulin Radioimmunoassay, Melani's 1970 Serum C-Peptide Separation & Modern Two-Antibody Electrochemiluminescence
item.description: How an unexpected antibody artifact became the foundation of clinical endocrinology: Berson & Yalow's (1956-1960) competitive radioimmunoassay (where rising unlabeled hormone lowers the bound-to-free tracer ratio), Melani, Rubenstein & Steiner's (1970) detection of equimolar co-secreted C-peptide in human serum, and modern two-antibody electrochemiluminescent C-peptide testing in insulin-treated patients.

item.title: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
item.description: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

item.title: How the ECG Learned to Follow You Home — Waller's 1887 Limb Recordings, Einthoven's Calibrated Quartz String Galvanometer, Holter's 1961 Portable Tape Recorder & Barrett's 2014 24-Hour vs. 14-Day Patch Comparison
item.description: From bedside galvanometers to ambulatory rhythm monitoring (H041): Waller's (1887) limb-contact control ruling out mechanical chest movement, Einthoven's (1903) calibrated string galvanometer, Holter's (1961) portable battery-powered recorder, and Barrett et al.'s (2014) paired 146-patient comparison showing why the adhesive patch's diagnostic advantage over 24-hour Holter monitoring (96 vs. 61) came from extended sampling duration rather than Day-1 superiority (52 vs. 61).

item.title: How One Breath Tests Gas Transfer — Marie Krogh's 1915 Paired Breath Samples, Ogilvie & Forster's 1957 Helium-Dilution Single-Breath DLCO & Roughton-Forster Membrane vs. Red-Cell Partitioning
item.description: From Marie Krogh's 1915 diffusion experiments to modern single-breath DLCO (H043): paired breath-hold sampling, Ogilvie & Forster's (1957) inert helium tracer dilution separating airspace mixing from true vascular uptake, Roughton & Forster's (1957) serial membrane and erythrocyte resistance model, and clinical interpretation of DLCO, VA, and KCO.

item.title: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
item.description: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

item.title: How a Treadmill ECG Tests the Heart Under Load — Master's 1929 Two-Step Test, Bellet's 1961 Radio-Telemetry Exercise Recording, Bruce's 1963 Multistage Treadmill Protocol & the Duke Treadmill Score
item.description: From two-step challenges to multistage exercise stress testing (H042): Master & Oppenheimer's (1929) standardized step workload, Bellet et al.'s (1961) radiotelemetry during exercise vs. recovery, Bruce et al.'s (1963) graded multistage treadmill protocol, and Mark et al.'s (1987, 1991) Duke treadmill score integrating exercise time, ST deviation, and symptoms.

item.title: How a Sealed Booth Measures the Air Left in Your Lungs — Hutchinson's 1846 Vital Capacity Spirometer, DuBois's 1956 Boyle's-Law Body Plethysmograph & Trapped Emphysematous Gas vs. Helium Dilution
item.description: From Hutchinson's 1846 spirometer to DuBois's 1956 body plethysmograph (H043): why standard spirometry cannot measure residual volume, applying Boyle's pressure-volume law across a closed airway shutter inside a sealed cabin, and why plethysmography captures non-communicating bullae and trapped emphysematous gas missed by single-breath helium dilution (Bedell et al. 1956; O'Donnell et al. 2010).

item.title: The Cocaine Signal That Stayed Behind — Cocaine-Associated Chest Pain, Serial hs-cTnI Trajectory, Human DAT-Cocaine Cryo-EM (PDB 9EO4), Benzoylecgonine/Cocaethylene LC-MS/MS & Lange Vasospasm
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

item.title: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

item.title: The Blue Dye & the Oxygen Number — Methylene Blue, Acquired Methemoglobinemia, Two-Wavelength SpO2 vs. Co-Oximetry & G6PD Limits
item.description: How an industrial phenothiazine dye became the antidote for acquired methemoglobinemia—and why both ferric methemoglobin (660/940 nm) and intravenous methylene blue itself spoof two-wavelength pulse oximeters toward an ~85% plateau while multiwavelength co-oximetry separates fractional species.

item.title: The Calabar Bean & the Missing Signal — Physostigmine, Acetylcholinesterase Ser203 Carbamylation, Antimuscarinic Delirium & QRS Counterfactuals
item.description: From Efik esere ordeal records in Old Calabar and Thomas Richard Fraser's Edinburgh experiments to human acetylcholinesterase Ser203 carbamylation (4EY4/1GQR), false-positive urine TCA immunoassays, and ECG QRS gating in antimuscarinic delirium.

item.title: The Tree That Stayed in the Timber — Forensic Timber STR & Chloroplast Profiling, Koompassia Log-to-Stump Matching, Shorea Databases & UNODC Likelihood Ratios
item.description: Forensic botany and timber DNA identification: matching three seized Koompassia malaccensis logs (L75, L79, L80) to stump S12 across a 1,465-tree Malaysian reference database (Lee et al. 2025), Shorea leprosula population (45.9%) vs. regional (88.7%) self-assignment across 1,410 trees (Ng et al. 2022), chloroplast vs. nuclear STR inheritance (Ng et al. 2017), Eucalyptus DNA and dendrochronological exclusion (Roman et al. 2020), and UNODC (2016) likelihood-ratio principles.

item.title: The Alarm Beyond the Wall — Post-Storm Portable Generator Exhaust Aerodynamics (167 Florida Cases, 16 Outdoor vs. 16 Garage), Wind-Wake Infiltration, Pulse Oximetry SpO2 Blindness & Battery CO Alarms
item.description: Forensic investigation of post-storm portable generator carbon monoxide infiltration: 2004 Florida hurricane hospital/CPSC records (167 nonfatal cases in 51 incidents; 16 outdoor vs. 16 garage generators), aerodynamic wake infiltration through windows and window AC units, two-wavelength pulse oximetry SpO2 optical blindness vs. CO-oximetry, and North Carolina ice-storm battery-backed CO alarm survival evidence.

item.title: The Potassium That Rose in the Tube — Reverse Pseudohyperkalemia in Leukocytosis, Pneumatic Tube Shear vs. Hand-Carried Whole Blood, Cold-Induced ABCB6 Leak & ECG Sensitivity Traps
item.description: Dissecting in-vitro potassium artifacts before the analyzer: Mansoor et al. (2015) reverse pseudohyperkalemia (9.5 mmol/L across three analyzers vs. 3.7 mmol/L on hand-carried whole blood due to pneumatic-tube mechanical lysis of fragile leukemic white cells in heparinized plasma), Xiong et al. (2022) familial cold-induced ABCB6 red-cell potassium leak, and Raffee et al. (2022) why a normal ECG cannot rule out true hyperkalemia.
